rationale: Response A is substantially better because it treats the migration as a workflow-and-incentive change, sequences a credible beachhead and champion-led rollout, defines reproducibility operationally, and proposes direct outcome measures such as independent time-to-reproduce. Its deliberate non-goals are disciplined and proportionate to ninety days. Response B has useful adoption and organisational insights, but its plan is internally inconsistent and operationally unrealistic: it proposes standing up JupyterHub, MLflow, shared storage, and Slurm or Kubernetes within weeks while claiming to avoid overbuilding; assumes unobtrusive automatic provenance capture without explaining the considerable integration work; dismisses even lightweight CI; and recommends deleting researchers’ local copies, an unnecessarily coercive and risky measure that conflicts with its voluntary-adoption strategy. A is therefore more sound, actionable, and calibrated.
